name: Pest control routing & compliance
hypothesis: Chemical-use logs + route optimization + license expiry tracking; mid-tier FSM doesn't fit cleanly.

market_sizing.target_buyer: Owner-operator or operations manager of a 2-25 technician pest control business. Decision-maker is typically the licensed principal technician who also handles compliance.
market_sizing.business_count_au: 2,924 Building Pest Control Services businesses in AU (IBISWorld 2025-26, +0.9% YoY). Industry revenue ~A$1.9B. Realistic SaaS-serviceable subset (excluding sole traders unwilling to pay $100+/mo and the large 50+ tech operators on PestPac/FieldRoutes) is ~1,500-2,000.
market_sizing.business_count_global: US ~30,000+ pest control establishments (IBISWorld); UK ~3,500; CA ~3,000. Global TAM ~40,000-50,000 SMB pest operators. US market matures fastest (PestPac, FieldRoutes, ServSuite, Briostack dominant).
market_sizing.typical_size: 3-15 technicians, A$600K-A$5M annual revenue. Owner often holds the principal licence and rides along.

pricing_reality.incumbent_pricing: GorillaDesk from US$49/mo (entry); ServSuite legacy plans US$126 / US$186 / US$339/mo before quote-only switch; PestPac and FieldRoutes are custom-quote, typically US$150-400/mo per user equivalent at SMB scale; Briostack mid-tier. In AU, generic tradie tools (ServiceM8, Tradify, AroFlo) used as poor-fit substitutes at A$50-A$150/mo.
pricing_reality.willingness_to_pay: AU realistic ACV A$150-A$350/mo for 3-10 tech operators, scaling to A$500+ for 15-25 tech. Compliance/license-expiry value-add justifies premium over generic FSM. Apply ~75% AU discount vs US list.
pricing_reality.sales_motion: Inside sales with demo + 2-week pilot. AEPMA trade-show booth and state-association partnerships drive top of funnel. Self-serve trial for sole traders.
pricing_reality.expansion_revenue_potential: Strong: per-technician seat expansion, customer-portal payments (Stripe), termite-warranty insurance referral, chemical-supplier rebate marketplace, AI-driven route optimization (premium tier). Embedded fintech via consumer payment plans for termite treatments (A$3-10K invoices). Plausible 2-2.5x ARPU lift.

competitive_landscape.incumbents: 1) PestPac (WorkWave, US) — legacy 30+ year incumbent, custom quote, heavy and dated; 2) FieldRoutes (US, now ServiceTitan company since 2022) — modern but US-centric, custom quote, $250M R&D backing; 3) ServSuite by FieldRoutes — same parent; 4) Briostack (US) — mid-market, route-optimization complaints; 5) GorillaDesk (US, ~US$49+) — SMB self-serve, light on AU compliance; 6) Fieldwork (US) — newer entrant with chemical tracking; 7) AU/local: Rapid Inspect (termite inspections), Pest Aware, plus generic ServiceM8/AroFlo. No AU-native end-to-end pest platform of scale.
competitive_landscape.incumbent_age_years: PestPac founded ~1985 (40+ years); ServSuite founded 1996; FieldRoutes (formerly PestRoutes) founded 2012; Briostack 2014. Two of the top three are 25+ years old with documented UI rot.
competitive_landscape.user_satisfaction_signals: Capterra/G2: Briostack — 'route optimization is horrendous, spending hours fixing routes monthly/daily'; PestPac — 'poor customer service', 'less value for price', 'archaic interface'; FieldRoutes — generally better reviewed but 'expensive for small operators' and 'support response slow post-ServiceTitan acquisition'. AU-specific complaint: 'no APVMA permit/chemical mapping', 'no NSW EPA record-keeping template', forcing technicians to keep parallel paper or Excel logs.
competitive_landscape.recent_funding_or_ma: ServiceTitan IPO Dec 2024 ($TTAN) consolidating FieldRoutes + Aspire under one parent; $250M R&D commitment announced at Ignite 2025. WorkWave (PestPac parent) PE-owned (IFS / EQT). No major net-new pest-control SaaS raise identified mid-2025-2026 in AU. Briostack acquired by ServicePro / Anstar 2020. Consolidation phase, not greenfield VC.
competitive_landscape.ai_disruption_risk: Moderate-high. FieldRoutes is shipping AI route optimization, predictive scheduling, and AI dispatch via ServiceTitan's R&D pipeline. AI-native challenger window is narrowing — likely 12-18 months before AI features become table stakes.

opportunity_quality.core_pain: Three unsolved-in-AU pains: (1) compulsory chemical-use record keeping under NSW Pesticides Regulation 2017 Part 4 (and equivalents in VIC PHW Act, QLD Health Pest Management) — technicians keep paper logbooks or Excel; existing US software doesn't model APVMA PubCRIS permit numbers, active constituents, or AU pest+host taxonomy. (2) Technician licence expiry tracking — VIC technician licences expire 3 years, trainee 12 months, NSW 5 years; missing a renewal halts revenue; spreadsheets dominate. (3) Daily route optimization across spread-out suburban jobs with chemical-mix-by-stop constraint; mid-tier FSM lacks chemical-aware routing. Today's stack: ServiceM8 + Word .docx safety data sheets + paper logbooks + Xero.
opportunity_quality.moat_source: Regulatory data moat: APVMA PubCRIS sync, state-by-state record-keeping rule engine, audit-ready export. Workflow moat: chemical inventory tied to technician licence + job + customer + state regulation. Network effect via shared chemical-mix recipes and SDS library. Switching cost via 7-year audit retention requirement.
opportunity_quality.critical_integrations: Xero / MYOB; Stripe (consumer plans for termite); APVMA PubCRIS chemical database; NSW EPA / QLD Health / VIC DHHS technician licence verification (manual or scraped); SafeWorkAustralia SDS; Twilio SMS; Google Maps / Mapbox for routing; Cliniko-style customer portal.
opportunity_quality.incumbent_ehr_lock_in: Low. No EHR-equivalent owns pest data. Customer data lives in PestPac / Briostack but exports cleanly; switching cost is workflow not data lock-in.

build_difficulty.regulatory_complexity: High. Each AU state administers its own pest-management licensing and pesticide regulation (NSW EPA, VIC DHHS, QLD Health, WA Health, SA Health, TAS DPIPWE) with different record-keeping templates, retention periods (typically 4-7 years), notification rules (community notification for outdoor spraying), and trainee/principal/technician licence tiers. Federal APVMA controls the chemicals themselves (label rates, off-label permits).
build_difficulty.regulatory_changes_2025_2026: APVMA is mid-review of 21 active constituents including all four neonicotinoids (clothianidin, imidacloprid, thiamethoxam, acetamiprid) — proposed regulatory decisions rolling out Dec 2025 through Oct 2026. Each decision can change permitted uses, label rates, and record-keeping fields overnight, creating churn-forcing events that favour a software vendor who ships rule updates fast. NSW EPA continues to tighten compulsory record-keeping audits. WHS Code-of-Practice updates and PFAS-related restrictions also pending. No single 'July 2026 cliff' like NSW eCoC, but rolling compliance pressure throughout the window.
build_difficulty.domain_depth: Moderate-high. Outsider can ship MVP with 2-3 design partners but must internalise APVMA label structure, state record-keeping schemas, and termite-warranty workflow. ~3-month domain ramp before credible product.
build_difficulty.mvp_effort: 5-8 months for solo/small team (jobs, customers, properties, technicians + licences, chemical inventory, application records, routing v1, Xero, customer portal, audit export). Chemical rule engine + state matrix is the long pole.
build_difficulty.technical_risks: Route optimization at scale (incumbents struggle — see Briostack); offline-first mobile for rural job sites; APVMA PubCRIS data ingest (no clean public API — needs scraping or PDF parsing); multi-state rule engine maintenance; SDS storage/version control.
build_difficulty.state_by_state_variance_au: High. Six state regulators + federal APVMA. Record-keeping fields, notification thresholds, licence categories, and renewal periods all differ. Rule engine per state is mandatory; this is also a competitive moat against US incumbents.
build_difficulty.data_residency_requirement: Soft. Not legally mandated, but auditors and government clients (council pest contracts) prefer AU hosting. Supabase ap-southeast-2 sufficient.

distribution_difficulty.channel_options: 1) AEPMA annual conference + state chapter events (peak body, ~A$5-10K booth); 2) State-by-state pest-management association sponsorships (NSW PCA, etc.); 3) Industry magazine Professional Pest Manager (paid sponsorship slots); 4) Facebook: 'Australian Pest Control Operators', state groups; 5) MPL Training Centre and registered training organisations as channel for new-licensee onboarding; 6) Cold outbound (licensed technician registers are partially public via state regulators); 7) Google Ads on 'pest control software Australia'.
distribution_difficulty.trade_association_count_au: ~6-8 (AEPMA national, AWPMA women's chapter, plus state pest-management associations in NSW, QLD, VIC, WA, SA).
distribution_difficulty.trade_publication_count: ~3-5 (Professional Pest Manager magazine, AEPMA newsletter, industry trade press; smaller universe than electrical/plumbing).
distribution_difficulty.industry_facebook_group_size: Small-mid. 'Australian Pest Control Operators' and state-level groups total ~5,000-15,000 members estimated; smaller and more tight-knit than electrician/plumber communities.
distribution_difficulty.conference_event_count_au: 1-2 main (AEPMA Conference annual, state chapter events). Under-$10K booth attainable at state level; AEPMA national booth ~A$10-15K.
distribution_difficulty.cold_outbound_viability: Moderate. NSW EPA, QLD Health publish licensed-technician details partially (lookup by name); business ABN + Google Maps yields company contacts. Verified email enrichment via Apollo viable. Phone outbound highly effective in this trade.
distribution_difficulty.founder_market_fit_proxy: Moderate. Owner-operators trust insiders but will give outsiders a chance if compliance pain is acute. Co-founder or paid SME from AEPMA strongly recommended.
distribution_difficulty.case_study_acquisition_cost: Moderate. 5 reference customers in 8-12 weeks via direct outreach to AEPMA members + free pilot exchanging logo rights. Slower than mobile mechanic; faster than e.g. funeral directors.
distribution_difficulty.content_seo_competitiveness: Low-medium. 'Pest control software AU', 'APVMA chemical log software', 'NSW EPA pesticide record template' are rankable in 6-9 months. US incumbents do not target AU SEO.
distribution_difficulty.insurer_or_gatekeeper_dependency: Moderate. Termite warranty insurance carriers (Rapid Solutions, Termguard) are key gatekeepers if expanding into warranty issuance — they restrict integrations to accredited platforms. Core product viable without them. State regulator licence verification can be manual initially.

personal_fit.manuva_data_model_reuse_pct: 55-65%. Direct reuse: tenant + RLS, auth, activity_log, customers (= properties + bill-to), suppliers (= chemical suppliers), inventory items + bins (= van + warehouse chemical stock with batch/expiry), purchase orders, stock movements (= chemical applications). New: technician licences, properties (with GPS + history), application records (chemical + rate + target + area + WHP), routing engine, APVMA chemical master.
personal_fit.manuva_code_reuse: Auth, tenant context, RLS, activity logging, server actions, Xero/MYOB scaffold, design system, batch/expiry inventory model — all transfer. Chemical batch + expiry tracking maps cleanly to Manuva's existing inventory invariants.
personal_fit.buyer_persona_overlap_with_manuva: Very low. Manuva manufacturers and pest operators share zero customer base. Fresh GTM motion required.
personal_fit.adjacency_to_manufacturing: Low. Field service / route-based / compliance-heavy is a different world from process manufacturing. Inventory + batch concepts are the only shared muscle.
personal_fit.technical_moat_durability_months: 12-18 months. Compliance + chemical rule engine + state-by-state matrix is non-trivial to replicate even with AI coding tools. Integrations (APVMA, payments, Xero) and accumulated compliance corpus are the durable moat.

unit_economics.gross_margin_sensitivity: Healthy. Some Mapbox/Google Maps usage (routing), Twilio SMS notifications (pass-through). AI route optimization may eat 3-5% margin if hosted on premium AI infra; mitigated via OR-tools self-hosted. Expect 78-85% gross margin.
unit_economics.multi_location_natural: Limited. Most pest businesses stay single-depot. Multi-state expansion exists but rare. Seat-based pricing per technician is the growth lever.
unit_economics.churn_risk: Low-moderate. Compliance lock-in (audit retention, licence records) creates stickiness. Annual churn 8-15% plausible once past first year. Sole traders churn higher.
unit_economics.customers_needed_for_target_arr: ~280-320 customers at A$270 ARPU to hit A$1M ARR.
